summary: TiCx films were deposited using atomic layer deposition (ALD) with tetrakis–neopentyl–titanium as the precursor and H2 plasma as the reactant. The films exhibited high conformality, low resistivity (~600 lΩ cm), and excellent step coverage (~90%) over nano-scale trenches. The study highlights the successful use of a nitrogen- and halogen-free metallorganic precursor for ALD of TiCx films.
evidence: TiCx films were deposited by atomic layer deposition using tetrakis–neopentyl–titanium [Ti(CH2C(CH3)3)4] and H2 plasma as the precursor and reactant, respectively. The growth of the rock-salt–structured TiCx films was confirmed by X-ray and electron diffraction. The C-to-Ti ratio determined by Rutherford backscattering spectrometry was ~0.52 and the film resistivity was as low as ~600 lΩ cm with a high density of 4.41 g/cm3. The step coverage was approximately 90% over the trench structure (top opening diameter of 25 nm) with an aspect ratio of ~4.5.
